note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, authored none of the change). RFC 7854 Section 4.10: "Sent OPEN Message: The full OPEN message transmitted by the monitored router to its peer. o Received OPEN Message: The full OPEN message received by the monitored router from its peer." 238bdb62e9 (spec-refuse-instead-of-defaulting) changed PeerInfo/StructuredEvent PeerAS from uint32 to rpc.RemoteAS; the unit now writes rpc.RemoteASOf(N) where it wrote N, the same known peer AS, and no assertion, input byte or expected value changed (TestHandleSenderStatePeerUp, TestPeerUpOnCacheMissNeverReachesTheCollector). The second unit now builds its per-peer header through the test helper mustPeerHeader, which calls peerHeaderFromEvent and fails the test on its new refusal; the event has a known AS, so the written frame and the assertion that no Peer Up without both OPENs reaches the collector are the same. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. Re-judged 2026-10-13 after the RFC 7854 Section 3.3 guard (no Peer Down for a peer never reported up). Positives unchanged: TestHandleSenderStatePeerUp and TestBMPSenderPeerUp echo both cached OPENs byte for byte. Negative TestPeerUpOnCacheMissNeverReachesTheCollector: up event with no OPEN cached, down event, then a Route Monitoring sentinel on the same FIFO queue; the first message read must be the sentinel, and a Peer Up is a named failure. Owner-approved marker change (sentinel replaces the Peer Down, which Section 3.3 no longer owes). Reviewer observed red with the guard removed (first message became the Peer Down), so the test still sees the whole queue head; a Peer Up emitted without both OPENs would be read first and fail.
